items.title: Verse Four: Craving as Smoke Before the Fire, and the Arhat Untouched by Gain or Loss

items.zh: 無不普燭；諸天世人惟當讚美，不應譏論。又能超度生老病死。如是故言：若計勝等劣，彼遂興諍論；於三種無
items.en: Having severed craving and pride towards name-and-form, without attachment, the smoke stilled; free of affliction, free of expectation — such [qualities] are not to be seen among either gods or humans, in this world or the next.
unmoved, for them equal, superior, and inferior are all absent.

items.zh: 言名色者，謂五取蘊。若有於彼觀見為苦，當諦現觀於五取蘊盡見苦時，於五取蘊所有貪愛，由意樂故皆說為斷，非隨眠故。彼若即如己所得道轉更修習；於其我慢無餘斷滅，成阿羅漢，諸漏永盡。
items.en: "Name-and-form" refers to the five aggregates of clinging. One who observes them to be suffering, upon directly realising the truths and seeing the five aggregates entirely as suffering, is said to have severed all craving towards them — in disposition, though not yet in every latent trace. Continuing to cultivate the very path already attained, one's residual pride is finally extinguished without remainder, and one becomes an arhat, all defilements forever exhausted.

items.zh: 由已證得阿羅漢果，心善解脫，便於自身、自身眾具、纏及隨眠皆悉永斷，離愛、離憍、離諸放逸。彼由如是離愛、離憍、離放逸故，名煙寂靜。無有燒惱，亦無悕望。云何名為煙寂靜耶？煙名為愛。何以故？
items.en: Because they have realised the fruit of arhatship and their minds are well liberated, they have cut off for ever attachment to their own body and its possessions, and the entanglements and latent tendencies; they are free from craving, free from arrogance, free from all heedlessness. Because they are free from craving, arrogance, and heedlessness in this way, they are called 'with the smoke stilled'. They have no torment and no longing. Why is it called 'the smoke stilled'? Smoke means craving. Why?

items.zh: 如世間煙，是火前相，能損眼根，便為擾亂，令不安住。愛亦如是，是貪瞋癡火之前相，能損慧眼，亂心相續。謂能引發無義尋思。彼於此愛，已斷已知，乃至令其於當來世成不生法，名煙寂靜。
items.en: Just as, in the world, smoke is the precursor of fire, injuring the eyes and disturbing them, leaving them unsettled — craving is just the same: it is the precursor of the fire of greed, hatred, and delusion, injuring the eye of wisdom and disturbing the mind's continuity, giving rise to thoughts devoid of benefit. One who has severed this craving and fully understood it, so that it will never arise again in future — this is called "the smoke stilled."

items.title: Verse Four Closes: Free of Expectation, and a Virtue Found in No Other Realm

items.zh: 彼既如是煙靜離著，雖復追求命緣眾具，非不追求；然能解脫貪愛追求，所求無染。云何無惱？謂彼如是現追求時，若他自施，或勸餘施，施時殷重非不殷重，精而非麁，多而非少，速而非緩，然不愛味。於所得物無染受用，不生耽吝乃至堅著。如是受用命資具時，不為貪惱之所燒惱。若彼施主自不能施，或障餘施，設有所施，現不殷重，不現殷重，乃至遲緩而不急速，然不嫌恨。由此因緣，不生恚惱。又於受用所得物時，不慼不念，無損害心及瞋恚心。如是不為瞋惱所惱。又於所得若精若麁，於受用時，深見過患，善知出離，安住正念，遠離愚癡。如是不為癡惱所惱。云何無悕？悕名悕望，繫心有在。彼不擎鼻內懷貪願，往趣居家。謂剎帝利大宗葉家，或婆羅門、長者、居士大宗葉家。我當從彼獲得上妙應所噉食，乃至財寶、衣服、餚膳、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥供身什物。如是追求及與受用，於此財物都無悕望。
items.en: Such a one does not go to a household harbouring a craving wish, as an elephant lifts its trunk towards what it wants... thinking, "I shall obtain from them the finest food, wealth, clothing, delicacies, bedding and seating, and medicine for illness." In seeking out and making use of such things, there is no expectation towards this wealth at all.

items.zh: 又彼恒常安住死想。謂過夜分入晝分中，復過晝分還入夜分，於其中間我有無量應死因緣，如經廣說。所謂發風，乃至非人之所恐怖。由此因緣，所為追求、所為受用所有財物，於此壽命亦無悕望。
items.en: And such a one constantly abides in the perception of death — knowing that, whether passing from night into day or from day back into night, there exist in the interval countless conditions by which one might die, exactly as the sutras describe at length: a disturbance of the wind-element within the body, and so on, up to being terrified by non-human beings. For this reason, in seeking out and making use of any wealth, there is no expectation towards life itself either.

items.zh: 如是無著、煙寂靜、無燒惱、無悕望故，於此天人、帝釋、自在、世主天等所有因中都不可見。於彼天人諸因果中，亦不可見。又於此四洲天人世間，及彼餘處都不可見。又於此世界天人世間，及彼餘處都不可見。
items.en: Being thus free of attachment, the smoke stilled, free of affliction, and free of expectation — this is nowhere to be found within the causal paths of gods, humans, Śakra, the lord of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven, or the great Brahmā king; nor is it found within their resulting states. Nor is it to be found among the gods and humans of these four continents, or in any place beyond them. Nor is it to be found among the gods and humans of this world-system, or in any place beyond it.

items.zh: 如是故言：斷名色愛慢、無著、煙寂靜、無惱悕、不見此彼天人世。復次，初頌顯示待時諸欲，於欲邪行及邪行果。第二頌中，顯示捨欲應正道理，淨修梵行仍被譏論不應道理，及待時欲。如第二頌，第三亦爾。第四頌中，世尊顯示現所證法永離熾燃，乃至智者內自所證。又初頌中，宣說諸欲是應說相，顯待時欲。由彼諸欲，非纔須時即便稱遂；要以言說為先，然後追求受用。又顯於彼由想安住不了知故，起於邪行，及招生死邪行果報。第二頌中，顯於諸欲能了知故，離邪願故，修梵行故，離邪見故，離見根本我慢種故，遠離耽著利養恭敬故，棄捨諸欲應正道理。由此因緣，他所譏論不應道理。又顯諸欲是待時性。所以者何？
items.en: Therefore it is said: 'Having cut off craving and pride in name-and-form, without attachment, the smoke stilled, without torment or longing, one is not seen in this world or the next, among gods or humans.' Further, the first verse shows sense pleasures that depend on time, wrong conduct in sense pleasures, and the result of that wrong conduct. The second verse shows that giving up sense pleasures accords with reason, that criticising one who purely practises the holy life does not accord with reason, and that sense pleasures depend on time. As with the second verse, so too with the third. In the fourth verse, the World-Honoured One shows that the dharma realised in this life is free for ever from burning, up to what the wise realise inwardly for themselves. Further, the first verse teaches that sense pleasures are what should be spoken of, and shows that sense pleasures depend on time: they are not obtained the moment one needs them; first there must be speech, and only then are they pursued and enjoyed. It also shows that because one rests in perception and does not understand them, one engages in wrong conduct and incurs birth and death, the result of wrong conduct. The second verse shows that giving up sense pleasures accords with reason, because one understands sense pleasures, leaves behind wrong aspirations, practises the holy life, leaves behind wrong views, leaves behind the seed of self-conceit that is the root of views, and leaves behind attachment to gain and respect. For this reason, criticism by others does not accord with reason. It also shows that sense pleasures depend on time. Why?

blocks.text: The fourth verse describes the arhat: one who has cut craving and pride towards name-and-form, whose "smoke is stilled", and who has no expectation. A long passage at the end of today's reading (0371c22–0372a09) is missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises it.

"Name-and-form" here means the five aggregates of clinging. Seeing them as suffering, at direct realisation of the truths one cuts craving towards them "in disposition". Master Cháng Bǎi: at stream-entry the afflictions arising from views are cut, but not the seeds of innate afflictions. Only by continuing to cultivate, until pride is extinguished without remainder, does one become an arhat.

"Just as, in the world, smoke is the precursor of fire, injuring the eyes", so craving is the precursor of the fire of greed, hatred, and delusion, injuring the eye of wisdom. "The smoke stilled" is craving severed so that it never arises again.

The arhat still has a body and must seek food and robes. Master Cháng Bǎi: "it is not that he does not seek them; but he no longer has craving towards them." Venerable Miào Jìng: those who are not noble live for the sake of craving; the arhat lives without it.

"Free of expectation" (無悕): Master Cháng Bǎi explains the image of "lifting the trunk": an elephant raises its trunk towards what it wants to eat. The arhat has no such reaching. And the arhat "constantly abides in the perception of death", aware that any night or day may be the last; yet, Venerable Miào Jìng adds, arhats do not take their own lives; they depart when life ends.

Such virtue is found among neither gods nor Brahmā. Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm gods still crave pleasure; Brahmā is attached to meditation; his four immeasurables are a worldly path that leaves the seeds of affliction intact.

The prose restates the verse ("having cut craving and pride towards name-and-form, unattached, smoke stilled, without vexation or expectation, he is not seen in this world or the next, among gods or humans"), then sums up the four verses: the first shows desire's proper time and the fruits of sexual misconduct; the second, the faults of grasping desire; the third, freedom from pride and dispute; the fourth, the arhat's freedom.

quiz.q: In "having severed craving and pride towards name-and-form," what does the treatise say "name-and-form" means?
options: the fourth link of dependent origination
quiz.why: "Name-and-form refers to the five aggregates of clinging." Observing them as suffering, upon directly realising the truths one is said to have severed craving towards them in disposition.

quiz.q: The treatise says craving is severed "in disposition, though not yet in every latent trace." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this?
options: at stream-entry only the 112 conceptually arisen afflictions of the four truths across three realms are cut — the disposition is severed, the seeds not yet
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at stream-entry one severs only the 112 conceptually arisen afflictions pertaining to the four truths across the three realms — the disposition is cut, but the seeds are not. Only by continuing to cultivate the path already attained, extinguishing pride without remainder, does one become an arhat.

quiz.q: In comparing craving to smoke, what points of likeness does the treatise draw?
options: smoke precedes fire and stings the eyes; craving precedes the fire of greed, hatred, and delusion, injures the eye of wisdom, disturbs the mind, and gives rise to useless thoughts
quiz.why: "Just as, in the world, smoke is the precursor of fire, injuring the eyes... craving is just the same: it is the precursor of the fire of greed, hatred, and delusion, injuring the eye of wisdom and disturbing the mind's continuity." Severing craving so that it never arises again is "the smoke stilled." Venerable Miào Jìng: the eye of wisdom is a second, inner eye — and the more important one.

quiz.q: Having stilled the smoke, does an arhat still seek food, clothing, and other requisites? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: the karmic body remains, so to sustain life he still seeks requisites — but without craving or defilement towards them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: since the karmic body remains, to sustain life the arhat must still seek food, clothing, and the other requisites — it is not that he does not seek them; but he no longer has craving or defilement towards them. Venerable Miào Jìng: those who are not noble ones live for the sake of craving, while the arhat seeks without taint.

quiz.q: The treatise says the arhat does not go to a household "lifting the trunk" with a craving wish. What does 擎鼻 mean?
options: an elephant raising its trunk to hook food into its mouth — an image of grasping reach
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when an elephant wants to eat, it lifts its trunk to hook things and bring them to its mouth — this is "lifting the trunk." Venerable Miào Jìng: the elephant raises its trunk towards what it longs for. In seeking and using requisites, the arhat has no expectation towards this wealth at all.

quiz.q: Why, according to the treatise, does the arhat have no expectation even towards life itself?
options: he is weary of the world and wants to die
he has already gained long life
he constantly abides in the perception of death — between night and day there are countless conditions of death, from a disturbance of wind to fright from non-humans
quiz.why: "And such a one constantly abides in the perception of death" — passing from night to day or day to night, there are countless conditions by which one might die. Venerable Miào Jìng adds that arhats do not take their own lives; they follow conditions and depart when life ends.

quiz.q: The treatise says this freedom is found in neither the causes nor results of Śakra, the lord of the highest desire heaven, or Brahmā. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: the gods have never heard the Dharma
the gods' lives are too short
Brahmā's causal practice, the four immeasurables, is a worldly path with seeds intact; in result, desire-realm gods still crave sense pleasure and Brahmā craves his meditation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm gods still crave sensual pleasure, and the great Brahmā king is attached to his meditation; Brahmā's practice of the four immeasurables is a worldly path that leaves the seeds of affliction intact. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the causes" means their thought and conduct.
